Aura Residue 
These rules are presented for the Game Master to incorporate if he sees 
fit. Magic in the form of spell use, magic-item use, or activation of 
magical powers can leave behind a minute trace of Aura, called Aura 
residue. This residue is only a fraction of a point, and thus cannot be 
collected to be brought into the pool. The length of time the residue 
remains depends on the amount of Aura used; it is suggested that the 
residue last for one day per point of Aura put into the spell. If more 30 
or more Aura points are put into a spell it will be permanent. This 
magical residue can be removed with a successful Absorb Aura roll. 
Aura residue can reveal the following properties with a critical success 
of a Detect Aura skill roll: 
1) The Aura Level of the original spell, magic item or power. 
2) The types of magic used in the spell (energy, death, etc.) 
3) Optionally, a signature trace that identifies the caster could be 
seen on the Aura itself. This could be used to track spell usage. 
Learning Spells from Residue 
A spellcaster with the spell Duplicate Spell, Detect Aura and Absorb 
Aura could learn the magic of a spell from its residue by the following: 
1) A critical success Detect Aura needs to be rolled. 
2) A Duplicate spell is then cast on the residue. 
3) Absorb Aura is rolled to remove the current residue. 
4) The spell is recast the spell with Duplicate Spell. 
5) The caster must spend the same Aura as the previous spell. 
6) A 1/2 Scroll Knowledge roll must be made.

The recipes for transmutation of one substance into another will 
generally be more costly than locating the substance itself. Even so, 
such recipes should exist (at least by rumor) and allow the skiJI user to 
search for and ultimately acquire them. The Game Master must be 
careful to make the recipe costly enough that the transmutation process 
does not overbalance the game. If lead can be easily and inexpensively 
changed to gold, then soon gold will loose all meaning and the econo-
my, such that it is, will collapse. A formula should alter the skill 
chance depending on how complete each is and what the intended 
effect of the Transmutation is.

spell effects do so at an Aura Level equal to 2x the creator's Title.

equal or less than the anti-toxin (a type 14 anti-toxin potion would

potion lasts 2d6 hours, half that time in vacuum.

HERMETIC LORE 
Magic in raw form may be all around the fantasy set-
ting and most wouldn't even know it. Magical crea-
tures have magical parts; in stone, earth, wood, crystal, 
and metal can be found all kinds of magical properties. 
These raw magical materials are called hermetic, and 
can be used to cast spell or make magical concoctions 
(such as with Elixir). 
Casting Spells with Hermetic 
The skill user collects basic hermetic materials, and 
when he wishes to cast a spell, combines them together 
and makes a Hermetic Lore skill. Success indicates the 
spell is cast. A base hermetic material is required to be 
used as a medium, in addition to the one material based 
on each of the 16 types of magic used in the spell (see 
the type reference in each spell heading).

Aura Control starts at 2 when Hermetic Lore is acquired and increases 2 per Practitioner Title, just as Scroll Knowledge does. 
However, Aura Control for Hermetic Lore is not the same Aura Control used for Scroll Knowledge. A character can only ever have 
one Aura Control, and thus cannot have two skills which give an Aura Control. Regeneration Rate is not a factor, because none of 
the skill user's Aura is utilized by Hermetic Lore. The usual limits based on Practitioner Title of the caster still apply. See the magic 
section for a full explanation of casting spells with Hermetic Lore. 
Modifiers to Skill Rolls 
The Hermetic Lore skill roll is modified by the strength of the base material as well as the weakest material being used. The adjust-
ment to the casting time will also modify the chance. Casting times are considered to be the casting time listed with the spell or 5 
seconds, whichever is greater. Round up when taking a fraction of the casting time.

RUNE LORE Expanded rules 
Runes are based on the metaphysical principle of meta-signa-
tures. A meta signature ties the physical world and the magical 
world together in a specific point. Runes must be inscribed 
onto a surface with a special form of writing called "rune 
script". The rune is only as permanent as the substance with 
which it was inscribed. Thus water-based substances can wash 
off, but a rune chiselled into stone can last for centuries. This 
makes the skills Stone Lore, Wood Lore and Metal Lore espe-
cially useful with runes. 
Time to Inscribe 
Inscribing a rune involves more than simply transcribing it onto 
a surface. As the rune is being created, it must be magically 
"seared" onto the surface as well. This is literally the process 
of burning magic into the physical rune. This process takes up 
to one hour per rune to do properly. If the practitioner is 
rushed, there will be a reduced chance of the magic "sticking" 
to the rune. The Rune Lore chance is reduced by 1 % for each 
minute under 60 by which the practitioner shortcuts the process 
(no less than l minute can ever be spent). Thus if the practi-
tioner only spends 40 minutes instead of the full hour, his skill 
roll will be at a -20%. lf he spends the minimum time of l 
minute, his chance will be at -59%. 
Types of Inscriptions 
Runes can be inscribed with three different methods. The 
method of inscription does not change the effect of the rune, but 
it does determine how the rune will work. Some of these meth-
ods of inscription make the rune more powerful, and thus 
change the rating of rune, decreasing the Rune Lore skill 
chance. The three methods of inscription are: 
Type 
___ 
Rating Modifier 
Emanating 
none 
Perceived 
+2/-10% 
Radiatino 
+4/-20% 
Emanating runes affect only the thing on which they are 
inscribed, therefore they do not need to be viewed by anyone in 
order to work. Thus a Rune of Power could be inscribed on a 
Mage's body as an emanating rune and it would affect the Mage 
while under his robe. 
Perceived runes work only when touched or perceived visually 
by a being. Just as magical songs must heard to take effect, 
perceived runes must seen. If a person is blind or refuses to 
look at the rune, it will not take effect on that person. However, 
if the rune enters the field of vision of a character for any rea-
son it will then take effect (this is left to the Game Master's dis-
cretion, but generally between 90 and 180 degrees). Perceived 
runes do not affect the being on which they are inscribed. 
Radiating runes are the most powerful, as they work on any-
thing which the rune can "see". Thus if an unobstructed 
straight line can be drawn from the rune to any part of a being, 
the being will be affected. The rune will not affect the being or 
surface upon which it is inscribed. The rune recognizes other 
meta signatures and then resonates metaphysically to generate 
its effect. Radiating runes cannot have their effect when cov-
ered up. A radiating rune can be given a "sight distance"; this 
means that it will only affect beings who come within this 
range. Every radiating rune is considered to have a base sight 
distance of 1 foot. This distance can be increased, and will 
increase the rating of the rune by + 1 per 5 feet (thus reducing 
the total chance by 5% per 5 feet of sight distance).

A rune can be inscribed in all three ways and will have all three 
abilities, i.e. it can be an emanating, perceived, and radiating 
rune all at the same time. In this case all rating/skill modifiers 
are cumulative. For example, the Flame Rune is both a per-
ceived and a radiating rune; it is not emanating (otherwise it 
would burn whatever it was inscribed upon). The effect of the 
Flame Rune works when a being sees the rune (perceived), but 
it will also work if the being walks within 1 foot of the rune, 
whether he perceives it or not (radiating). 
Activating runes 
Meeting the conditions necessary to cause a rune to take its 
effect (seeing a perceived rune, etc.) is said to "activate" the 
rune. A rune can be inscribed so that its activation will be 
delayed (even when the normal conditions have been met) until 
a word has been spoken or deed has been performed. The rune 
will not begin working until after all these conditions have been 
met. For example, a Flame Rune could be inscribed so that it 
will only activate when someone says "flame". Thus an indi-
vidual might view the rune or walk within 1 foot of the rune, 
but it would not activate until someone said the word "flame". 
Adding this condition to a rune raises its rating by +2 (-10% to 
total chance). It should be noted that the activation condition 
will only work when used with runes inscribed on non-moving 
objects; moving any object with such a rune on it will activate 
the rune. 
Ongoing Effects of Runes 
Any rune which adversely affects a being will re-activate once 
every 10 seconds, as long as the being continues to meet the 
conditions necessary to activate the rune. For example, the 
Flame Rune causes a person to burst into flames like the spell 
Produce Fire. This effect will occur again every 10 seconds as 
long as the being remains under the effects of the rune. 
139 

===== PAGE 150 =====
Destroying and Dispelling Runes 
A rune will last as long as the substance that was used to create 
it. The power of a rune can be destroyed by destroying the 
writing material or medium. For example, if a character drew a 
rune onto his body with an oil based substance, and this sub-
stance was scrubbed off, the rune would no longer work. If the 
rune was chiselled into stone, then the mark in the stone would 
have to be destroyed by chiselling it away or warping it beyond 
recognition with Stone Lore, etc. Runes are Aura based, and 
can be dispelled with the spell Dispel Magic or any appropriate 
dispel spell (a rune of protection could be dispelled by Dispel 
Protection, etc.). The chance of being dispelled is a contest of 
magics, where the amount of Aura put into the dispel x 5% is 
rolled against the rating of the rune x 5%; however, the person 
attempting to dispel the rune always has a -50% modifier. 
Runes will also be absorbed by Walls of Protection and the like. 
Re-enchanting an inscription: If the magic of a rune is dis-
pelled, this does not destroy the physical inscription. For exam-
ple, a rune would still be chiselled into stone even after its 
magic was dispelled. In this case, the rune can be re-enchanted 
onto the same exact location it was before without having to 
chisel out a new inscription. Such runes have only a base time 
of 30 minutes to re-inscribe at a +20% chance, with the same 
time modifiers as above (-1 % per minute less than 30). Thus if 
a rune has been tattooed onto a body and was dispelled, it could 
be re-enchanted in half the time.

The runes listed in the Player's Guide and the Master's Manual 
have already had their methods of inscription determined, and 
their ratings reflect this. However, if a player wishes, he may 
customize these runes by changing the methods of inscription as 
explained above. The following is a list of these runes and 
what method of inscription is used to create their effects:

Greater Runes 
Almost any rune has the ability to be inscribed as a greater rune. A 
greater rune has double the abilities of the normal rune and must be 
inscribed at a +8 rating. For example, a Greater Rune of Power would 
give the user +6 to Aura Control and be rating 30. Each greater rune is 
considered to be its own rune, and is subject to the limits on runes. 
Note that for some runes, doubling the effect does nothing and so there 
is no greater rune. 
Limits on Runes 
The following limits should be placed on rune usage: 
1) No more than one rune may be on the practitioner per Goal. 
2) In addition, no more than one rune per Goal may inscribed 
on any objects or exterior structure per Goal of the practitioner. 
10th Goal, a Rune Lore practitioner could have 10 runes 
inscribed on his body and 10 runes inscribed on objects external 
to his body.

Starting Spells 
Some characters other than Mages may start with a positive 
Scroll Knowledge chance (possibly as a non-acquired skill) and 
may have a positive Aura Control because of bonuses from 
Intelligence and/or the social skill Metaphysics. If the character 
will eventually receive Scroll Knowledge (or Spell Lore) as a 
class skill, he should begin with one one spell for each of the 
skills with a positive base chance. Mages should begin with 
I d4+2 spells, or one per 10% of their Scroll Knowledge chance. 
The GM can choose the spells or roll randomly from the tables 
on pages 226-227 of the Player's Guide. A Mage should begin 
with a balance between offensive, defensive and utility spells. 
Regardless of Aura Control, only cantrip level spells are given 
to starting Mages (levels 1-4). 
Access to Scrolls and Spell Notes 
It is important that a spellcaster has the opportunity to acquire 
spells. This is up to the GM, but a good rule of thumb is about 
three new spells per Goal. Eventually a spellcaster will be 
unable to memorize all of the spells in his book, but he will 
have options that force him to make decisions in preparation for 
adventures. These spells should be given out in an interesting 
manner, not necessarily dumped onto the character seemingly 
from out of the sky. Spellcasters in a party will usually trade 
incessantly among themselves so probably any spell given to 
one spell caster will likely end up given to all. Some options 
for where spells can be found:

Periodic study of one spell may grant understanding of 
another. Usually a Spell Lore skill roll is made to achieve 
this but you may want to add bonuses and/or chance against a 
common Spell Lore skill with liberal modifiers. 
With the spell Duplicate Spell it is possible to catch a spell 
and then to learn it within a limited amount of time. Combined

Notes on the Runes Spell 
The runes spell allows a caster to create copies of a spell that 
can be cast by any who can read it. These rune scrolls count as 
active external spells for the caster who made them. It is there-
fore not possible for a caster to create hundreds of these scrolls 
141 
to pass out to an army. Additionally, once a person reads this 
scroll and casts the spell, he is now considered the caster and 
thus is subject to the active spell rules. This means that charac-
ters who have a O Practitioner Title in Scroll Knowledge cannot 
have any active spells and thus are limited to only those spells 
which take immediate effect, such as Finger of Fire. 
Rules for Spellcasting 
A spellcaster can cast spells in any form as long as the form has 
arms, digits and good vocal ability. The caster must have at 
least one hand free to perform the gestures. 
Spellcasting in armor: Any class with Scroll Knowledge can-
not cast spells when wearing armor outside of the class's armor 
usage parameters. The ability to cast spells in armor can be 
gained when Armor Lore is 100%. Thus if a character with 
Scroll Knowledge had Armor Lore at 100%, he would be able 
to cast spells in armor for suits which he had Armor Lored. 
Penalties to hit with missile spells: Some missile spells require 
that the caster make a successful intelligence sav.e to hit an 
opponent. In these cases, the Game Master may wish to apply 
any penalty that would normally apply to a combat attack by 
translating every +/- 1 into a +/- 5% modifier to the save. 
Creation Spells and Social Skills 
Any spell which produces a physical product, such as Produce 
Metal, Produce Wood, etc. will normally produce only a basic 
shape of the substance. When combined with a social skill, 
however, the caster can make an object of highly detailed quali-
ty. For example, casting Mend or Repair on a suit of armor will 
make a metallic blob where the armor was damaged. However, 
if the caster makes an Armoring roll, the suit could look like it 
once did. This should be left to the GM to use creatively, and 
can be used to explain why certain warriors would not want 
Mages repairing their armor. Another example would be the 
spell Produce Food. Without a successful Cooking roll, the 
spell will make a generic food substance that although will pro-
vide sustenance, will be tasteless and unappetizing. This princi-
ple can be applied throughout the system, and comes down to 
the fact that a character cannot make that which he does not 
know.

Mastering the Aspects 
Aspects are broken into two categories: aspects of focus, and 
aspects of action. 
Focus aspects: These are the aspects which define that part of 
the spell which is the focus, or the substance being affected. 
They are denoted in the diagram by solid black circles. 
Action aspects: These are the aspects which define how the 
focus of a spell is acted upon, or how the substance is affected. 
They are denoted by black rings. The focus aspects sit within 
the action aspects. An action aspect can only affect a focus 
aspect if the black circle denoting the focus aspect lies inside 
the ring denoting the action aspect. 
Characters must follow a path when choosing aspects to master. 
A character must first choose a focus aspect (black circle) to 
master. From there, he must master all of the action aspects 
(rings) which can affect that focus. Once all of these action 
aspect have been mastered, the character can then master a new 
focus aspect. Once he has mastered this new focus aspect, he 
must master all action aspects which can affect that focus 
(which he has not already learned). Note that creation and dis-
placement are overlapping rings, but are still separate aspects 
which must be mastered individually. This pattern continues. 
The only exception is for focus aspects outside the action rings 
(sensing, illusion, warding, meta). A character cannot master 
one of these focus aspects until he has mastered all of the action 
aspects. 
Example: A character masters the focus aspect energy. He then 
must master the action aspects of creation, displacement and 
alteration, as these are the aspects which energy lies within. He 
can then choose a new focus aspect. At this point he could 
choose illusion, sensing, warding, or dimensional. Lets say he 
chose to master natural. He must then learn all action aspects 
which can affect natural; because these are the same as the 
three he has already mastered, he can proceed on to a new focus 
aspect. Lets say he then chose mind. Before he can master a 
new focus school, he must next master control and transference. 
He has already mastered alteration, and so may now choose a 
new focus aspect. 
Bonuses for Specialization 
If a character has mastered all of the aspects associated with a 
spell (listed in the "Type" heading with the spell), he will gain a 
+3 Aura control when casting that spell. Additionally, for each 
aspect of the spell which has been mastered, the character gains 
a bonus of+ 10% to his Scroll Knowledge chance when 
attempting to learn the spell. 
Penalties for Specialization 
When the specialization rules are in effect, the character has a 
-10% chance for to his Scroll Knowledge chance for each 
aspect he has not mastered in a spell when attempting to learn 
that spell. In addition, the character has a -3 Aura Control when 
using a spell that has aspects which he has not mastered. 
GM note: There are several ways to implement specialization. 
One way is to use only specialization rules, so that all spellcast-
ers have specific flavors. Another way is to set a Title where a 
character must choose to specialize or not, after which the 
option is no longer available. This will prevent abuse of the 
specialization rules.

SPELL LORE 
A spell user with Spell Lore can master a spell much like a 
weapon user with Weapon Lore can master a weapon. When a 
spell caster gets Spell Lore he is immediately afforded mastery 
of one spell and consequently gains improved ability with all 
spells. Thereafter, at each achievement of Title the player may 
make a Spell Lore skill roll to master one new spell. Any spell 
that the Spell Lorist creates himself with this skill (see the Spell 
Creation System) are at an automatic +30% chance to be mas-
tered. If the Scroll Knowledge specialization rules are in effect, 
the practitioner can only master a spell for which he has mas-
tered all the aspects. Effects for worlds allowing spell masters 
are listed below. 
Spell Mastery Effects 
•General: +2 Aura Control for all spells after learning Spell Lore. 
•For Any Mastered Spell: 
1) The caster has +2 Aura Control with the spell. 
2) The area affected can be changed when cast so long as it 
does not increase. No dimension can be decreased more than 1/4 
distance (this allows for basic shape changing). 
3) The range and distance to focus of the spell can be increased by up 
to 3 times normal distance. 
4) The duration of the spell can be doubled (instantaneous of 
course still remains instantaneous) 
S) The spell may be made permanent as per the spell Permanency at 
1 /2 the Will Force cost regardless of whether the spell caster 
has the spell Permanency or not. 
6) +20% to all saves/resistances involving this spell if the spell caster 
has it used against him. 
7) No somatic gestures are needed to cast the spell; only verbal. 
8) Mastered spells can be taught to students at +20% to the students 
Scroll Knowledge roll. 
9) All others are -20% to any saves/resistances required by the spell. 
10) The caster cannot be intetTUpted by loss of concentration unless he 
takes a wound which reduces him to negative Endurance in an area. 
11) The casting time of the spell can be halved (round up). 
Creating New Spells 
With this skill a spellcaster can research and invent his own 
spells. Many good spells in Imagine were created by player 
character spell lorists. Nothing excites a player more than to 
come up with something truly unique to express themselves. As 
long as a spell is not unbalancing and the proper research crite-
ria have been met, it is a good idea for the GM to allow new 
spells into his game (use the Spell Creation Guide in the Design 
section). 
WJLDMAGJC 
See the Skills section and the Spell Creation Guide for more 
details. 
ltlus,ons 
illusions are magical, and thus directly affect the spirit of a 
being. The spirit then tells the mind that an effect is happening, 
and the mind may or may not be fooled (thus Illusion 
Resistance is based on a mental attribute, Wisdom). If fooled, 
then the mind creates a psychosomatic injury to resolve the par-
adox in reality. This is called illusionary damage. 
Illusion should appear to behave exactly like the real thing they 
are simulating (no swords passing through arms, etc.) except for 
the people who know that it is illusionary. Damage is assessed 
as listed in the Player's Guide tables, except that the GM 
records that it is only illusionary damage. Damage should be 
applied to the body area that was struck, and when the character 
gets to negative Endurance in an area, he makes all the same 
saves that he normally would for combat; thus he may fall 
unconscious, or think he cannot use a limb. If the injury would 
kill him, instead of dying the GM rolls for heart attack damage 
as listed in the PG. 
GM can allow a perception test (or perhaps relevant skill roll) 
to detect the odd occurrance. In this case the victim of the illu-
sion could make a new Illusion Resistance roll, possibly with a 
bonus of say 20%. These new rolls are up to the discretion of 
the GM. 
The GM should first allow Illusion Resistance to be made at the 
request of the player. After an initial roll is made, a new one 
can be made every 5 seconds. Sometimes the character never 
suspects that there is an Illusion, and in these cases it is up to 
the GM if he wishes to allow the characters to have an Illusion 
Resistance roll when they start to notice odd things. Odd things 
would be in cases where an TI!usion is only partially complete, 
such as an illusion of a warrior who made no noise whatsoever 
when he moved (because Illusion of Sound was not be used). 
Thus the most powerful illusions are those which have all the 
elements of an illusion (sight, sound, taste, etc.) and thus proba-
bly never give the character any reason to doubt the reality of 
the illusion. Sometimes too many illusions lead to players 
requesting Illusion Resistances at everything they see. In these 
cases, the rules for insanity (simple schizophrenia) should be 
used, as the character is losing the ability to distinguish between 
reality and illusion. Hints can be given that the character is 
starting to go insane,giving the player a chance to stop asking 
for resistance rolls all the time. 
See the Player's Guide for the amount of damage done by 
Illusions.

he realm of divine magic stands outside all other 
forms of magic. It is the power of the deities, 
and as such its control is primarily in the hands 
of the Game Master. Powers can be taken with 
Divine Denial from characters who do not follow 
the wishes of their deities. However, the benefit of using such 
power is that it is subtle, and often unable to be influenced or 
affected by skills that involve Aura magic, as well as the fact 
that divine magic users can call upon supernatural aid through 
communing. The following guidelines should help players and 
GM's alike to use the divine skills and powers in the Imagine 
Role Playing System™. The GM should see the Setting section 
for designing specific deities. 
Supernatural Servants and Summon Supernatural 
Throughout the lifetime of the Divine Knowledge practitioner, 
he is receiving aid in the form of invocations. Usually these 
invocations are not granted directly, but instead are granted 
through a hierarchy of supernatural servants that serve the deity. 
When summoned they may aid the higher Title divine magic 
users directly. The maximum number of servants provided by 
the deity is based on the practitioner's Summon Supernatural 
Practitioner Title:

This is not to say that the practitioner can call them all at once 
or will necessarily know each and every one of her supernatural 
servants right away. They often appear for the first time when 
they are needed and then offer their name and service to the 
divine worshipper. It is up to the GM to provide the creatures 
and supernatural beings that are summoned with skills like 
Summon Supernatural. The being should be something which 
fits the appropriate deity and his realm of influence. Servants 
can be created with the Creature Creation Guide in the Design 
section. 
Supernatural Definition 
All beings from other planes, deities, servants, planeswalkers, 
etc. are considered supernatural for purposes of detection, sum-
moning, and other skills involving the supernatural. Undead do 
have a supernatural element, but it is up to the individual GM 
whether or not undead are to be lumped in with other forms of 
supernatural (it is recommended that they are, especially the 
more powerful ones). The basic rule is that if something is not 
not from the earthly plane of existence, it's supernatural. This 
can mean that normal beings appear as supernatural to the 
denizens of the outer planes. 
Supernatural Invocation Usage 
Any supernatural servant, semi-deity, deity, supreme deity, etc. 
has unlimited usage of any of the invocations it provides to 
other beings. A being may not provide an invocation to a being 
whose Title is higher than its level or Title. 
Banishment from a Plane 
When a being is banished from a plane of existence he is ban-
ished for 1 month per 5% of the skills success, unless the GM 
has another scheme or reason to set a duration. 
Wounds on Other Planes 
Most wounds from other planes will heal at a rate of 1/3 of all 
wounds per day of rest on the being's home plane. Three days 
of rest equals a complete healing unless special circumstances 
are involved: i.e. cursed wounds, etc. 
Death on Other Planes 
No supernatural being can be truly killed unless he is killed on 
his home plane. When the being is killed outside his home 
plane, he vanishes and his body returns to a safe place on his 
home plane. There he will slowly be returned to life after three 
days. 
True Names 
Each being in the game world should have a true name. A 
being's true name is specifically definable by the GM for his 
world. While a being's true name may be a secret organization-
al name, birth name, or combination thereof, the true name may 
be so secret that the individual may not know it himself.

Spiritual Writ Invocation 
The invocation Spiritual Writ allows a caster to create copies of 
an invocation that can be read by others. These writs count as 
active external invocations for the invoker who made them. 
Additionally, once a person reads the invokes the writ, he is 
now considered the invoker and thus is subject to the active 
invocation rules. This means that characters who have a 0 
Practitioner Title in Divine Knowledge cannot have any active 
invocations and thus are limited to only those invocations which 
take immediate effect. 
High Piety Invocations 
No invocations exist over 20 Piety level because the mortal and 
arch mortal is unable to wield that much divine power. 
155 

===== PAGE 166 =====
Divine Knowledge as a Non-Acquired Skill 
This is expressly denied. The deities are finicky and do not 
grant invocations before a being has been enlightened (gained 
the Divine Knowledge skill) even if her Piety Control is posi-
tive because of Wisdom bonuses or the social skill Theology. 
Converting to Another Deity 
Sometimes a character may want to begin following a different 
deity. To the average being this has no great effect, but to 
Priests and the users of divine magic this is special undertaking. 
The character must renounce their previous faith to their friends 
and companions, but most will make a public statement or com-
plete a ritual to join the new faith. When she has joined the 
new faith all divine skills are reduced to 0% chance and invoca-
tions are stripped from her. Title bonuses for commune are 
removed. She must commune (at the lower chance) everyday 
until either the god or one of her minions accepts the priest as a 
priest of the new faith. This may never happen or it may hap-
pen almost immediately (GM discretion). When it does, the 
Priest is granted a first mission, quest, atonement, act of faith, 
etc., which can be as small as converting a few more worship-
pers or as big as saving a cause. In this grace period, as it is 
called, all skills are at l/2 chance. Also, skills and invocations 
are used as if the Priest or divine user was 1/2 of her normal 
Title (rounded up). If the being completes all required tasks, 
skill chances and invocations can be returned to normal. 
Conr;RetJonal W oRShip 
Prayer Circles 
When two or more worshippers of the same deity or religion 
gather in the same place to pray or ask for guidance on a partic-
ular issue, the chance of communing is increased. The highest 
Piety individual leads the prayer and the other worshippers add 
their commune roll to this leader. The chance of commune can 
never exceed twice the normal commune chance of the prayer 
leader. However, if the prayer leader has a 0% commune he is 
at least afforded a l % if others join in. Similarly, priests or oth-
ers that share a divine skill can also add their skill ability (not 
the base) to a leader. However, the leader can never get a bonus 
of more than 20% by this method. Unlike commune, if the cho-
sen leader has a 0% chance in the divine skill, then secondary 
individuals afford no bonus. 
Temples, Churches, Holy Ground and Sacred Places 
These places can offer anywhere from a +5% to a +20% to 
divine skill usage and a +2% to + 10% to commune rolls, 
depending on the GM determined sanctity of the place. Asam-
ple is provided:

Example: A young boy is dying of a dread disease. The town 
loves him and brings him to the temple in hopes the gods will 
see pity on them and help the beloved boy. The temple priest 
has only a 15% chance to use the skill Cure Disease, as he has 
just acquired it from his experiences. He has 4 priests and 2 
priestess that help him care for the town. One of the priests 
also has a base 5% chance because he has not yet acquired the 
skill but has a high Piety. Another priestess has already 
acquired the skill and has a 12% total chance (base 5% chance 
plus starting bonus of 7% ). The sub-priest cannot help because 
he yet has no ability in the skill and the priestess can only add 
her starting bonus of 7%. Thus far the chance for the temple 
priest is increased from his original 15% to 22%. The priest is 
in the village church and this affords him another 10% bonus 
raising the total chance to 32%. There are 60 worshippers of 
the good god in the area around the temple. This increases the 
chance an additional I 0%. The total is 42%. The village prays, 
the GM rolls a 29%, and the boy is saved from likely death 
from the ravages of the disease he suffers. 
Spiritual Raiments 
Often a priest or servant may have a holy robe, cloth, or the 
like. Just as areas, weapons, beings and water can be blessed or 
blasphemed so the possibility exists (at the GM's discretion) to 
use Bless or Blasphemy on raiments to add to a worshipper's 
commune chance or relevant divine skill. This effect can be 
temporary, lasting one hour per Title of the individual blessing 
or blaspheming. Alternately, a Will Force point could be 
expended to make the effects permanent. If multiple raiments 
are worn only the greatest of them has effect. The effect of the 
raiment varies by the individual who created it. A +5% to 
divine skills and a +2 % to commune is awarded per full 5 
Titles of the practitioner who created it. 
Holy Water 
A Bless practitioner is limited to creating one dose of Holy 
water per Title per day; after this, divine denial ensues. Holy 
Water trapped within a divine item will not expire until the item 
is destroyed or no longer divine.
