Final body weight and size 
Now that you have the final body weight, you will use this number to 
determine its body size. Body sizes are subjective classifications that 
are not recorded on the creature form, but are used in the creation sys-
tem to determine a multitude of other factors. Record the body weight 
of the creature on the creation form, as well as a range you feel is 
accurate for the species of creature. This range can vary widely, but 
should be within a few pounds for smaller creatures, a few hundred 
pounds for medium type creatures, and a few thousand for enormous 
creatures.

Tree Attributes 
Non-mobile trees and other plants have an Agility listed as NIA. Any 
modifiers count as "O" that are derived from Agility; they are +10 to 
hit and x2 damage whenever they are struck. Moving trees should 
generally be in the lower Agility range. To determine size category, 
use the animal weights table above. 
Attributes 
After choosing attributes, it is a good idea to go through the abilities 
and see if the creature will have any that increase attributes before you 
compute all the values which are based on those attributes. Abilities 
which increase an attribute should be used for creatures which have a 
much higher value than other creatures of similar size, type, etc. 
Physical Attributes (Strength and Vitality) 
Unless the creature is magical or supernatural, the body type and phys-
ical attributes should correspond closely. Make the physical attributes 
match the size and likely speed and coordination of the average crea-
ture of its type. For example, a medium sized creature has a max 
Strength of 16 in the table below. If a medium creature was designed 
to be much stronger for its size, then the ability "Enhanced Strength" 
could be given, increasing Strength 1-3 points above the normal range.

Personal Attributes (Appearance, Charm, Social Class) 
Personal ataibutes are generally based on the state of the soul. Many creatures, 
such as animals, will simply have an "N/A" listed for personal attributes, as

they are thought of as having no souls. Having low personal attributes means 
that creature is either horribly repulsive or terrifying. If you wish to give an 
animal or similar creature personal attributes for flavor, feel free. Mindless 
undead such as zombies should always have extremely low personal attributes, 
but an undead such as a Vampire might have high personals.

Attack Notes 
At1acking with a creature is more than rolling the dice and adding dan1age. 
Tactics are highly importanl to Imagine combat, and how well a creature uses 
its combal abilities greatly increases its effectiveness. For example, charging 
offers x2 damage and diving offers x3 damage. Some crea1ures prefer to lie and 
wail and a11emp1 10 pounce on unsuspecting victims, while some anack in 
packs. Devise tactics for the creature and record them in the anack noles. 
Movement 
Creatures can have a multitude of movement types and rates, and the 
following is a list of these types. In order to have a specific type of 
movement, the creature must meet the requirements for that movement 
type. In some cases, these requirements are actual abilities which must 
be bought from the abilities lists. The actual numbers for these speeds 
can be found on the tables that follow the movement descriptions, and 
are based upon the size and relative speed of the creature for its size. 
Walking Speeds 
Walking speeds are the base speed from which all other speeds are 
determined. Though every creature should have a walking speed, only 
creatures with actual legs are considered to be walking. All other types 
will have the same movement rate, but it will have an appropriate 
name (waddling, crawling, etc.). Some animal abilities will modify 
base walking speed (such as hooves). In this case, the new walking 
speed is used to determine aJJ other speeds. 
Jogging Speeds 
Creatures which have a walking speed can also have a jogging speed 
which is x2 their modified base walking speed. This is the fastest 
speed which some creatures will have, and some creatures (such as 
slugs) will not even have a secondary speed .. 
Running Speeds 
Most creatures which have a legs have a running speed which is x3 
their modified base walking speed. 
Galloping Speeds 
Quadrupeds and some reptiles have a galloping (or sprinting) speed 
which is x4 their modified base walking speed. This speed does not 
necessarily apply to all such creatures, however. 
Flying Speeds 
Birds, Avians and Giant Insect/Spider flying speeds 
The animal ability Wings can be bought, which will give a creature a 
short flight ability (about 10 seconds of flying). Glide Wings will 
287 

===== PAGE 298 =====
allow for a descending glide, but only the abilities Flight or Magical 
Flight actually give a sustained flight speed. These creatures have a 
flying speed which is x4 their modified base walking speed. Note that 
the creature must have the ability Diving (Aerial), or else it must make 
dives at -30% to Agility saves (see p.173 of the Player's Guide). 
Swimming Speeds 
The base walking speed is only a swimming speed for creatures with 
no legs, sea mammals, fish and the like. When the ability Swimming 
has been bought, Fish, Reptiles, Snakes, Mollusks, Worms and Sea 
Mammals have a maximum swimming speed of x3 their modified base 
walking speed. 
Determine initial movement by the relative speed of the creature based 
on the body type of the creature. Next modify the speed by the size of 
the creature relative to a standard creature of that body type. 
Tiny Creature Movement 
Tiny creatures (mostly insects) have basic standard speeds, which can be modi-
fied if necessary if they are unusually fast or slow. Not all creatures will have 
all types of speeds.

Allimal Abilities 
Animal abilities may be chosen by any creature type other than plants 
and magical plants. These powers, when listed with an animal, may be 
evoked with the Evoke skill. Each ability lists with it any special mod-
ifications for the way it works when evoked as opposed to be used by 
the actual creature. If there is no separate Evoke entry, then the char-
acter gains the ability as listed. 'Damage for attacks is set by the crea-
ture size. All creatures are considered to have the normal five senses; 
taste, hearing, touch, smell, and normal sight (as listed on p.39 of the 
Player's Guide), unless disabilities are taken which weaken or remove 
them.

Title.

Evoke: + 1-3 Agility points. Cost: Listed on the Agility Attribute table.

action time. Cost: 10 PP.

creature size effects table). Cost: 5 PP.

the skill Berserking. Cost: 2 PP per + 10%.

color of the environment around it. Evoke: +20% to Blend, + I 0% to 
Move Unseen. Cost: 5 PP.

Plant Abilities 
Plant abilities can be given to plants, magical plants, or slimes, but not 
the other creature types. Plants can have abilities only from this list, 
but magical plants can have abilities from this list and from the magi-
cal abilities list. Slimes can have abilities from this list, the magical 
abilities list and the animal abilities list. New plant abilities can be 
created by the player as he sees fit, and an appropriate cost assigned. 
Absorption/conversion (plant): Can absorb any plant material and 
convert it to the plant's form ( I cubic inch per hour), thus healing itself 
at a rate of I Endurance per hour. Cost: 2 PP. 
Absorption (self): The plant can merge with other plants of it's type, 
i.e. grow together and become one plant. Cost: 3 PP. 
Acid Sap: The plant has a form of sap that is corrosive (doing ld4 
points per hour to all fleshy substances). It may also have stems or 
pitchers that can release and store this sap. These pitchers will often 
close automatically when touched or stroked. Cost: 6 PP. 
Bark, Sharp: Sharpened bark that causes 1-3 to areas contacting it. 
Cost: 2 PP. 
Bark, Irritant: (See Irritant). Cost: 5 PP. 
Bark, Poisonous: Venomed bark. Cost: 5 PP, plus Venom Cost (see 
Venom in magical abilities). 
Bark, Diseased: Bark carries a disease harmful to beings and animals. 
Cost: 2 PP plus Disease cost (see Diseases). 
Bark, Parasitic: (See Parasitic Agents). Cost: 5 PP plus agent cost. 
Chemical Conversion: A form of chemical or a compound (blood, 
sulfur, salt, etc.) can be converted by the plant directly into energy to 
replace photosynthesis. To a degree all plants absorb some nutrients 
through their roots but these plants can survive completely on chemi-
cals. Cost: 2 PP. 
Evergreen: Plant is green all year round and is not as effected by sea-
sonal variation. Cost: 0 PP. 
Fruit/Flower/Bud/Seed, Poisonous: As venom but in fruit form. 
Cost: 2 PP plus venom cost. 
Fruit/Flower/Bud/Seed, Diseased: Carriers a disease harmful to 
beings, animals. Cost: I PP plus disease cost. 
Fruit/Flower/Bud/Seed, Parasitic: (See Parasitic Agents). Cost: 2 
PP plus agent cost. 
Fruit/Flower/Bud/Seed, Irritant: (See Irritant). Cost: I PP plus irri-
tant cost. 
Heat Co11strictio11 vines, trunks, branches: Constricts based on con-
tacting heat (warm beings) does damage based on type of constricting 
plant fiber and number. Vines do ld4+ I per 10 seconds per vine, 
branches do 2d6+2 per 10 seconds, trunks do 3d6+3 per 10 seconds. 
Hide (Bark): From I point of hide per 4 Endurance to I point per 2 
Endurance, depending on the thickness. Cost: 2 PP per hide. 
Hide (Fibrous): I point of hide per 5 Endurance. Cost: I PP per 2 
points of hide. 
Irritant: Causes a rash within 24 hours of contact of a fleshy beings 
skin. Rash lasts 3d4 days and causes I point of damage per day if 
itched. Itching must be resisted with Will Force save or some form of 
topical lotion. Cost: 5 PP. 
Leaves, Sharp: Sharpened leaves or nettles that cause damage to areas 
contacted. Cost: I PP. per 1-2 points done 
Leaves, Irritant: (See Irritant). Cost: I PP plus irritant cost. 
Leaves, Venomous Venomed leaves. Cost: 5 PP plus venom Cost. 
Leaves, Diseased: Leaves carry a disease harmful to beings and ani-
mals. Cost: 2 PP plus disease cost. 
Leaves, Parasitic: (See Parasitic Agents). Cost: 5 PP plus agent cost. 
Light-based Regeneration: Regeneration of I point of damage, per 10 
minutes in full sunlight, to all wounded areas. Cost: 10 PP. 
Parasitic Agents (delivered by the mechanisms shown above): 
Parasitic, simple: Causes a parasitic infection in living beings. This 
parasitic infection is an advance form of disease allowing a Disease 
Resistance to avoid. Failure indicates a loss of 1-3 physical and 1-2 
mental for the duration of the infection. The infection duration varies 
Cost: Based on duration. Lasts ld4+1 days (4 PP), Jd4+1 weeks (8 
PP), I d4+ I months ( 12 PP), lifetime of the being (30 PP). 
Parasitic, mood altering (violent): A Disease Resistance is required or 
the being or animal becomes uncontrollably violent and sees all mov-
ing things as a threat; +50% to Berserking during this state. When 
ended (as Berserking) the rage will leave in ld4 minutes. Cost: 10 PP. 
Parasitic, mood altering (passive): A Disease Resistance is required 
or the being or animal becomes nearly catatonicaly passive. Mental 
facilities are halved. The being can be lead around but will take direct 
actions only after making an Intelligence save to do so and a Will 
Force save to overcome the passivity. This effect lasts ld4 hours. 
Cost: 8 PP. 
Parasitic, mood altering (paranoia): The being becomes deeply afraid 
and phobic. Anything that could possibly be a danger requires a 
Control Resistance. lf this fails the being has entered a state of fear. A 
further Will Force determines how the being reacts to this fear. lf 
made the being cowers but does not run. If failed the being runs until 
the danger cannot be seen or felt to be near. This effect lasts ld4 
hours. Cost: 6 PP. 
Regeneration (Complete): Any part of the plant can re-grow into a 
complete plant at ld4 Endurance per IO seconds per day if exposed to 
water and nutrients. This plant has no vital areas. Cost: 30 PP. 
Regeneration (Plant): Any severed areas of the plant will grow back, 
given enough food and water, at 5 Endurance per day. Cost: 5 PP. 
Regeneration (Root): Any trunk or stem of the plant can grow roots if 
exposed to water (ld4 endurance per day). Chopping up the plant usu-
ally results in many smaller plants taking root. Cost: 4 PP. 
Seasonal Dormancy: Most plants have a time (winter/fall) when the 
go into a dormancy, conserving their energy and no longer taking sub-
stance to any degree or growing. This is marked by a loss of foliation 
and a changing in color. Cost: 0 PP. 
Spores: The plant Releases spores. Spores require a Poison 
Resistance to avoid; if failed Id IO in lost seconds sneezing. A few 
( 1-5%) of beings and animals will be allergic suffering weakness of 
-(1-2) physical attributes for ld4 hours after exposure. Can release 
spores no more than once per week and most varieties do so once per

Magical Plant Abilities 
Magical plant abilities can be given to magical plants or slimes, but not 
the other creature types. New magical plant abilities can be created by 
the player as he sees fit, and an appropriate cost assigned. 
Absorption/conversion (animal): Can absorb living animals. First 
contact causes adherence to the plant. Strength save required to break 
free once per 10 seconds, -5% per foot of plant material covering/con-
tacting the being. Every minute I half cubic foot of animal is converted 
to plant matter (cannot absorb armor, etc.). Cost: 20 PP. 
Brain: This plant is self aware and has a brain in one of it's vital 
regions. Cost: 2 PP, plus mental attribute costs. 
Bark, Razor: Tiny surfaces as sharp do ld6+2 to all areas that contact 
them. Cost: 5 PP. 
Cellular Division: The organism is composed of cells large enough to 
see. Each cell counts as a body region. Cells can divide under stress, 
and when they do, Endurance is divided equally between them. 
Cost: 10 PP. 
Chill: Plant can draw heat from beings. Does ld4 damage per cubic 
foot of plant to beings contacting the plant and needs I hour to 
recharge per ld4 done. Cost: I PP per ld4 .. 
Electric: Plant can generate electricity. Does ld8 damage per cubic 
foot of plant to beings contacting the plant and needs I hour to 
recharge per d4 done. Cost: 4 PP per ld8. 
Fibrous Hearing: Through thin fibers on some stems/trunks the plant 
can "hear" (requires nervous system). Cost: 21 PP. 
Force of Wood: +30% to the Force skill if the plant controls its limbs 
(i.e. sapient and mobile). Can also cause I point of structural damage 
per minute. Cost: 5 PP. 
Growth Conversion: The creature can convert energy (cold damage, 
heat damage, etc.), any drained attribute rating (from the drain magical 
abilities; Drain Mental, etc.), or one cubic foot of a certain substance 
(stone, wood, etc.) into I years growth. Cost: LO PP per I years 
growth gained in the conversion (10 PP if a point of cold damage can 
be converted to 1 years growth, 20 PP if a Will Force can be converted 
to 2 years growth, etc.). 
Heat: Plant can generate magical heat. Does ld6 damage per cubic 
foot of plant to beings contacting the plant and needs I hour to 
recharge per d6 done. Cost: 12 PP per d6. 
Leaves, Razor: The leaves have sharpened edges that cause ld4+2 to 
all areas that contact them. 
Leaves, Sonic: Some of the plant's leaves are stiff and can be vibrated 
to produce a kind a song voice. Cost: rating of song(s) produced. 
Magical Acid Sap: Can release extremely corrosive sap causing JdlO 
per IO seconds to all objects that contact it. Can only release one dose 
per cubic foot of plant per hour. Cost: 5 per ld!O. 
Maw: The plant has a mouth that can be used to grind pray, usually to 
store in a central chamber for slow digestion. The mouth does damage 
based on the size of the plant. Plants can have more than one Maw. 
Cost: 5 PP per maw. 
Mobility: Plant has ability to move branches and even uproot itself. 
Speed and ability vary by plant (use guide). Cost: 80 PP. 
Nervous System: The plant has a animal like nervous system within 
its trunks/stems/leaves. It can sense and react to tactile stimulation 
more than just locally. (Some leaves and stems of plants are tactile' 
sensitive reacting locally when touched; this does not require a nervous 
system.) Cost: 3 PP. 
Parasitic, Massmind: The plant is the central agent in a massmind, if 
the plant has the Brain ability then it is the overmind. Each person 
who contacts this parasite must make a Control Resistance or be men-
tally converted to a massmind shared by the other victims of this plant. 
Cost: 80 PP. 
Parasitic conversion (plant): Upon touching the plant, a Disease 
Resistance is required; Failure indicates the being falls into a deep un-
wakeable sleep. The being converts into the plant type over the course 
of I d4+ I days. Cost: 60 PP. 
Parasitic conversion (food): Upon touching the plant, the failure of a 
Disease Resistance causes the being to fall into a deep sleep and die in 
ld4 hours. After death the body will quickly (ld4 more hours) decay 
into a rich fertilizer that is pulpy and seeps into the ground. 
Cost: I 00 PP. 
Parasitic mood altering (protect): Upon touching the plant, a Disease 
Resistance is required or the being or animal will feel intense protec-
tive feelings for the plant. If a Control Resistance fails as well then the 
being or animal will become a guardian for the plant and keep others 
from harming it, unable to leave the vicinity of the plant until control is 
broken or the plant dies. The effect lasts ld4 days per exposure. 
Cost: 40 PP. 
Plant Eyes: The plant has eyes or eye stalks that can sense visually 
(requires nervous system). Cost: 3 PP. 
Thick Roots: +20% to the Brace skill, as well as any saves or contests 
involving Agility or Strength against being moved or toppled. 
Cost: 5 PP.

Skills 
Giving skills to creatures: Any skill can be bought in PP for 1/2 the 
cost of its rating (round up). The skill gets its maximum starting 
bonus. Skills are considered innate, and do not require the concentra-
tion of the creature to perform. 
Enhanced [skill]: Any skill a creature has can be given a bonus. 
Cost: l PP per + I 0% for common and social skills, 2 PP per + 10% for 
restricted skills. In addition, if an ability is chosen which enhances a 
skill (such as Enhanced Hearing), then the creature should get that skill 
for free, with the bonus added to the common chance/starting bonus. 
Practitioner Title: Any time a skill needs a Practitioner Title or Class 
Title, use the level of the creature for both. 
Powers 
Giving powers to creatures: Some creatures have magical or divine 
magical powers, and these work just like magic item powers. Any 
spell or invocation can be given to creature as an innate power. They 
are, in effect, built in spells and invocations. Powers take 5 seconds to 
use, but since they are innate to the creature, the do not require concen-
tration or Aura. This means that the creature can take other actions 
while performing the power. Powers can be chosen from the spell or 
invocation lists. Powers can be added at the cost in PPs at the Aura 
Level of the spell or the Piety Level of the invocation; add I PP for 
each time per day it can be used beyond the first, up to 10. Beyond JO 
a power can be made to be "at will" for a 15 PP. 
Experience Value 
See Awarding Experience to determine Experience value. 
Alignment 
Only sapient creatures have alignments, and these are completely ori-
ented to the flavor of the creature. Sapient undead should almost 
always be evil. Supernatural servants the alignment of their deity. 
Special Notes 
Any unique information, such as parts used for hermetic lore or herbs.

SupeRnatuRaLSeR~ants 
These are beings who serve a deity and the worshippers of the 
deity. Supernatural servants serve as messengers, bureaucrats 
of power, mortal aid, scale-balancers, warriors, executioners, 
healers, prophets, guides, and the like. Below every great deity 
are ranks of minions who perform the often trivial, boring tasks 
deities don't want to personally deal with. Occasionally a mor-
tal is lucky or powerful enough to be loaned a servant or two, 
on a partial basis of course. Servants are usually provided to 
those who are granted the skill Summon Supernatural, or 
through use of invocations like Spiritual Warrior. Use the pages 
that follow to develop your own supernatural minions. 
Sometimes other deities themselves can be servants, depending 
on the pantheon. And remember, it is not just those arch mor-
tals who vie for godhead, sometimes it is an uppity supernatural 
minion that escapes the ranks and becomes a deity himself.

Giant, Mountain (Magical Humanoid, Level 7) 
This is the largest of the giant races, standing on average 18' tall and 
weighing in around two tons. The Mountain Giant, like its cousins, 
has magic laced within its bones allowing for amazing height. The 
mountain giant has an extremely slow metabolism and eats infrequent-
ly and can sleep for days at a time. Some Mountain Giants have been 
known to go into hibernation for years at a time if no food or other 
resources exist to feed them. Mountain Giants are a lonely race who 
often know few kin. They are incapable of producing offspring with 
other giants and as such are Likely to be completely alone when 
encountered. They can be of any alignment and can make valuable 
allies but are often capricious, attacking smaller beings on whim or for 
food purposes.

Cougar (Animal, Level 2) 
The Cougar (or Puma) is a mountain cat that prefers to live in 
high footlands or low mountains. They are a light brown color 
that blends in well with plains and dry brushland. They are 
excellent hunters but are generally solitary, picking their prey 
carefully. Cougars are raised by their mother and taught to hunt 
until they are old enough to fend for themselves. The most dan-
gerous cougar is a mother defending her young.

Electric Jelly (Slime, Level 3) 
The Electric Jelly is the product of a Size Change experiment 
gone horribly awry. This multi-celled organism is actually a set 
of very large and independent cells. Before it was expanded the 
Jelly was a simple form of life that lived off of bio-electric 
energy. Now it is a ravenous membranous set of near cubic 
cells that attack living beings to drain their fluids and electrical 
energies. If an Electric Jelly is damaged it may break into sev-
eral pieces as the cells separate. Every cell of an Electric Jelly 
is an independent eating machine. 
Habitat: Damp, wet, slimy dark places, preferring places where car-
casses can be found.

Griff on (Magical Animal, Level 5) 
The Griffon has a lower body and tail of a lion but the upper 
body, head and wings of an eagle. Its sharp beak and talons are 
dangerous, especially when they strike from the air. This crea-
ture is a cunning hunter but possess no more than an animal's 
intellect. Griffons see the Pegasi as mortal enemies and will 
attack them on site. It can sometimes be seen hunting together 
if mated or a larger threat pushes their territories together. 
Nothing is known of its origin but it is likely magic was used to 
tamper with nature to produce this odd flier. Perhaps this is 
why Wood Elves shun them as steeds, preferring instead the 
Giant Eagles, but for the Human Knight or Cavalier, the Griffon 
is the ultimate steed. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Griffon's mate once per season and a lay a 
clutch of exactly three eggs. This creature will fight viciously 
to the death to defend both the eggs and the hatchlings that 
arrive 4-5 weeks later. Griffon hatchlings reach maturity in 6 
months time. These eggs are highly sought after because a 
Griffon can only be trained if raised from a hatchling. They 
usually hunt alone within a territory of about 20 to 40 square 
miles. These aerial predators will eat any meat and hunt any 
creature or animal within their territory. They live 12 to 20 
years. 
Climate: Highland, humid continental, humid oceanic and

Wraith (Undead, Level 9) 
Wraiths are a form of undead with pure malevolence and hatred for all 
life. They enjoy tormenting and torturing the living and will often do 
so if not in any apparent danger to themselves. The Wraith will often 
find and use other forms of undead for its own ends, though it cannot 
make undead other than subservient wraiths from its victims. The 
wraith can travel far and wide in search of its victims and is not bound 
to any one place in most situations. The wraith grows from life energy 
it takes and is always hungry for more. Wraiths rise from the dead 
from those who have pure hatred in their hearts when they are slain. 
They can also be created by dark or magical means. 
Habitat: They prefer places that might contain other forms of undead 
they can control. Can be found in any location, however. They also 
enjoy skulking the phase plane looking for stuck phased beings.
